headline: Blue Origin recovers. SpaceX stumbles. Defense budgets swell.
deck: This week, Blue Origin resumes launches while the Space Force doles out hundreds of millions.

stories.head: Blue Origin finds its launch button, finally
stories.body: After a thorough investigation, Blue Origin has cleared the way to resume New Glenn launches. The company had been grounded since a failure earlier this year, but it appears they’ve finally located the elusive 'launch' button. With a backlog of customers waiting, this could be a much-needed boost for a company that has faced its share of delays.
stories.soWhat: If only finding the right button was the hardest part of launching a rocket.

stories.head: Space Force awards $437M for military satellite network
stories.body: The Space Force has awarded Viasat and SES a hefty $437 million for a military satellite network, reinforcing the trend of serious cash flow into space infrastructure. This contract is part of a broader push to enhance military capabilities in orbit, proving that the budget is indeed always on the table. With global tensions rising, expect more of these sizable contracts to flow.
stories.soWhat: If only Congress could be as decisive about terrestrial budgets as they are about space.

stories.head: True Anomaly raises $190M amid defense boom
stories.body: True Anomaly has successfully raised $190 million in a Series C funding round, bringing its valuation to $1.6 billion. The company focuses on co-orbital security and space domain awareness, sectors that are becoming increasingly vital as geopolitical tensions escalate. With DoD backing, this cash infusion signals strong confidence in their business model.
stories.soWhat: In space, cash flow trumps tech hype, and True Anomaly just proved it.

watchlist.title: NASA's reorganization impacts future missions
watchlist.body: NASA's recent restructuring could lead to shifts in mission priorities, potentially affecting upcoming contracts and partnerships.

watchlist.title: AUKUS partners ramp up space capabilities
watchlist.body: As Australia builds its dual-use space infrastructure, expect increased collaboration among AUKUS partners, which could reshape regional dynamics.

watchlist.title: Palantir's TITAN extension to influence ground ops
watchlist.body: With a $480 million extension on the TITAN program, Palantir's influence on military ground operations is set to expand, impacting procurement strategies.

watchlist.title: Hypersonic tests delayed again
watchlist.body: With hypersonic glide-vehicle tests slipping for the third consecutive quarter, the timeline for operational capabilities is becoming increasingly uncertain.

talent.statLabel: Week-over-week growth in resumes from primes to Series B/C
talent.head: Talent is leaving big-aero — and it's not about money
talent.body: Compensation is not the gating factor. The complaint, almost universally, is schedule risk — the inability to ship anything quickly, the half-decade gap between joining and seeing flight hardware, the meeting that exists to schedule the meeting. The startups absorbing this talent will, in two years, be hard to compete with on a level playing field.
